# Figure notes — elnino_2026_impacts_map

**Generated by:** `make_impacts_map.py` (matplotlib 3.10 + cartopy 0.24, Robinson projection centred 180°). Outputs: PNG (200 dpi) + PDF (vector).

## Provenance of content

Regions, impact descriptions, seasons, and confidence tiers are taken from the summary table of `../research/impacts-literature.md` (13 Aug 2026), a literature assessment with per-claim verification tags. Confidence ratings are Zeke Hausfather's IPCC-style assessments as documented there. Selection rule (to v4): regions rated medium confidence or higher; low-confidence regions (California, Sahel, Mekong) omitted. **Superseded in v5**: see below.

**v3 addition (15 Sep 2026):** "N & Central India — weaker summer monsoon · Jun–Sep 2027" added at the lightest (medium) tier with the ⚠/dashed flag, at Zeke's request for a company briefing deck. Dossier basis (§A2): the dry signal is rated low-medium — the ENSO–monsoon anticorrelation has weakened since the 1980s (Kumar et al. 1999), east-Pacific-flavoured events are historically less drought-effective (Kumar et al. 2006), and 1997 delivered a near-normal monsoon (hence the flag). The 2026 season's observed −12% deficit is a developing-year outcome, separate from this 2027 signal. This region sits below the map's original medium+ inclusion bar; if the map is reused for publication contexts, decide explicitly whether to keep it.

Flag semantics (v2, revised after expert review):
- **Dashed outline + ⚠** = the canonical signal underperformed in a recent strong event: E Australia (DJF 2023-24 +18.9% national rainfall after a dry SON; BoM), Peru/Ecuador coast (2023-24 ICEN peaked weak, deficits to −100%; IGP/SENAMHI), Yangtze (2016 decay-summer far weaker than 1998; Zhang et al. 2016).
- **Horn of Africa** carries a text note "(size set by Indian Ocean Dipole)" instead of ⚠ — the 2023 floods verified catastrophically; what failed was the ENSO *attribution* (WWA: no significant ENSO role), so a "signal failed" flag would be wrong. Magnitude is IOD-conditioned (Palmer et al. 2023).
- Amazon "drought + fire": the drought signal is high-confidence; fire outcome is partly policy-contingent (~95% of fires human-ignited — C. Nobre, quoted in Nature 656:290). Single fill shows drought confidence.
- W Pacific "sea-level fall" is qualitative by design — the 20–30 cm figure in circulation is secondary-sourced and is not printed.
- Footer GMST wording is deliberately "a strong candidate" (Berkeley Earth's phrasing), not "likely record"; CO₂ wording is "well above trend," not "record."

**v4 layout revision (22 Sep 2026):** layout only; polygons, fills, confidence tiers and flags unchanged. Map cropped to 47°S–62°N (Robinson, centred 180°; no region lies poleward of ~40°S/50°N), figure 15×7.7 in. Labels moved to open ocean with bold region names and leader lines ending in a dot on each region; the ⚠ flag now sits beside the region name. Legend moved entirely below the map, with a dashed swatch for the flag. Central America timing text changed from "Dec–2027" to "Dec–Feb & summer 2027" to match dossier §A10 (DJF 2026–27 dryness plus the 2027 canícula). Previous version backed up in the session scratchpad only.

**v5 model-informed revision (23 Sep 2026).** Shapes and region set revised using the September 2026 dynamical seasonal forecasts (13 models: 6 NMME + 7 C3S centres). Full method in `../model_patterns/METHODS.md`; evidence per region in `../model_patterns/REGION_REVIEW.md`; all edits approved by Zeke region by region. Fill colour is still the **literature** tier; model output sets only the shape (where ≥80% of models agree on the literature sign with |z| ≥ 0.5, clipped to a window around the literature region; `model_patterns/derived/model_polygons.json`).
- *Model-derived shapes:* Maritime Continent, Philippines, southern Africa, Amazon, N South America, NE Brazil, Central America & S Caribbean, W Pacific islands, Hawaii, Horn of Africa, SE South America, Gulf Coast & Southeast, Cuba & Bahamas, S California/US Southwest/N Mexico, southern China, Central Pacific islands.
- *Hand-drawn (indicative):* Yangtze and N/Central India (summer 2027, beyond all forecast leads); Peru/Ecuador coast (sign confirmed 13/13 but the 1° grid can't resolve the coastal plain); E Australia, Pacific NW, S India (no robust model support this year).
- *Removed:* Ohio Valley (models 1/13 dry, leaning wet; no warm signal).
- *New hatch flag:* S India / Sri Lanka NE monsoon: this year's models disagree (4/13 wet, z −0.28).
- *Split:* "Central America & Caribbean" → "Central America & S Caribbean: drought, Dec–Feb" plus new "Cuba & Bahamas: wet, Dec–Feb" (Giannini et al. 2000; models 13/13, z +2.6). The models do **not** support a wet Yucatán (z −0.44), so it is not named. "Summer 2027" dropped from the dry label pending resolution: the Americas search (research/lit_missing_americas.md) says the midsummer drought is a developing-year Jul–Aug feature with a wet Caribbean early season in 2027 (Chen & Taylor 2002), conflicting with dossier §A10.
- *Added:* S California, US Southwest & N Mexico, wet Dec–Mar, medium + ⚠ (see California below); N South America dry Dec–Feb; Philippines dry Dec–Apr; southern China wet Dec–May (clipped south of the Yangtze region to avoid overlapping a different season); Hawaii dry Nov–Mar. All at medium-high, with Crossref-verified citations in research/lit_missing_*.md.
- *Seasons revised:* Maritime Continent Sep–Feb → Sep–Dec (DJF signal fades, 9/13); E Australia Sep–Feb → Sep–Nov (Cai et al. 2011; models weak even in SON, 10/13, z −0.24).
- *Tier change:* Pacific NW high → medium-high (models: dry 10/13, z −0.21; warmth mostly trend).
- *California evidence* (`../model_patterns/hindcast/`): observed 1950–2025 SoCal JFM slope +24 pp of normal per °C NDJ ONI (r = 0.39); strong events (ONI ≥ 1.5) median 148% JFM, 6/8 above normal; NMME hindcast slopes ≈ observed (median ratio 0.97). **2015–16: 9/10 models forecast wet; observed 60% (DJF) / 68% (JFM) of 1991–2020 normal** (NOAA nClimDiv CA div. 6), hence ⚠. N California is left unshaded: the long-record relationship is weak (DJF r = 0.18, n.s.), though all 13 models lean wet this year.
- *Southern Africa* stays high, no flag: 1997–98 was a documented failure (Lyon & Mason 2007), but 2023–24, with a comparable +IOD (SON DMI +0.89 vs +0.98), produced the worst drought on record.
- Horn of Africa note: seasonal models have a documented IOD-related wet bias for the short rains (Hirons & Turner 2018).
- **Correction to dossier wording:** the "2015–16 near-normal SoCal" claim was cited to Jong et al. 2016, which predates the outcome. Station data give 60–68% of normal (below normal; near-normal only in tercile terms). Use the station numbers or Siler et al. 2017 (doi.org/10.1175/JCLI-D-17-0177.1).
- Everything reflects one forecast initialization (Sep 2026) and should be refreshed with the October run.

**v5.1 follow-up (23 Sep 2026, approved by Zeke):**
- *Pacific NW → "Interior BC, N Rockies & inland Northwest: dry, low snowpack, Dec–Feb", medium, model-derived.* The old hand-drawn WA/OR/ID polygon sat across a model *wet* signal (western Oregon) and a model *dry* signal (interior). Models: BC z −0.76 and Prairies −0.60, 12/13 dry. "Warm" dropped: the PNW warmth disappears once each model's own land mean is removed (z +0.10). Literature (research/lit_canada_nw.md, 10 DOIs Crossref-verified): Shabbar et al. 1997 find a DJF dry swath from BC to the Prairies; Clark et al. 2001 find coastal Columbia Basin snowpack turning positive in midwinter. Medium because Ropelewski & Halpert 1986 found no high-latitude precipitation signal and strong-event outcomes for BC were not verified. Caveat: temperature-sensitive Cascades snowpack could still suffer where precipitation is near normal (Mote 2006).
- *Central Canada warm winter, Dec–Feb, medium (new "warm" category, colour #D6604D).* The colour was CVD-checked against the palette: worst ΔE 18.7, deuteranopia vs dry-high. The model-robust region runs from Saskatchewan to Quebec under all three trend treatments, strongest near Hudson Bay (z +1.0 to +1.2). It is trimmed at ~79.5°W because the literature puts the El Niño core "just west of Hudson Bay" and treats eastern Canada as NAO-dominated (Shabbar & Khandekar 1996; Bonsal et al. 2001). The Quebec extension is model-only.
- *E Australia → "SE Australia (Victoria & Tasmania): drought, fire risk, Sep–Nov", medium ⚠.* Model-derived (13/13 dry, z −0.43). The rest of eastern Australia shows no signal. This matches the positive-IOD springtime mechanism for SE Australia (Cai et al. 2009; Ummenhofer et al. 2009). The ⚠ is kept conservatively.
- *S India / Sri Lanka → "Sri Lanka: heavy NE monsoon, Oct–Dec", medium, unhatched.* Models: 12/13 wet, z +0.70. Peninsular India shows no signal (6/13) and is dropped. No "models disagree" regions remain; the hatch code is kept.
- *Peru/Ecuador* hand-drawn strip redrawn to the coastal plain, since models are robustly dry over the Andes just inland.
- Caveat: the SE Australia and Sri Lanka sub-region boxes were chosen after inspecting the maps (selection effect). They are supporting evidence for shape refinement, not pre-registered tests.

**v5.2 (23 Sep 2026, approved by Zeke): S California, US Southwest & N Mexico, medium → medium-high, ⚠ kept.** The basis is the station record, *not* model agreement (models also agreed in 2015–16). NOAA nClimDiv CA division 6, all 8 winters with NDJ ONI ≥ 1.5 since 1950:
- 6 of 8 above normal and in the upper tercile, against a base rate of about 1/3. P(≥6 of 8 by chance) ≈ 0.02. RONI ≥ 1.5 gives the same 6/8.
- The two misses: 1965–66 (78% DJF / 32% JFM, the only lower-tercile case) and 2015–16 (60% DJF / 68% JFM; below normal but middle tercile because of skew).
- 1950–2025 slope +24 pp of normal per °C (r = 0.39); no evidence of saturation at high ONI.
- The Southwest / N Mexico part was already rated medium-high by research/lit_missing_americas.md.

Caveats: n = 8, and 2026 forecast Niño-3.4 lies beyond the observed range. This supersedes the dossier's August "LOW" rating for California; that rating leaned on the misattributed "near-normal 2015–16" claim (see the dossier correction above). NA map footer updated to "6 of 8 strong El Niño winters since 1950 were wetter than normal…".

**v5.3 (23 Sep 2026, approved by Zeke after a colleague's suggestion): Peru/Ecuador coast, medium ⚠ → high, no flag, Dec–May → Dec–Apr.** North coastal Peru/Ecuador rainfall is governed by local coastal warming (Niño 1+2), and the ⚠ reflected 2015–16 and 2023–24, when that warmth was weak or faded before the rainy season. The check is `model_patterns/peru_nino12_check.py` → `derived/peru_nino12.csv`:
- Observed mid-September Niño 1+2 is +4.6 °C in 2026, against +3.5 (1997), +2.1 (2015) and +2.6 (2023). CPC weekly OISST, 1991–2020 base.
- The NMME Sep-2026 forecast for Jan–Mar is +3.0 (range +1.9 to +5.1 across 6 models), and Feb–Apr +2.7 (range +1.6 to +5.2). The observed values were 1997–98 +2.3/+2.2, 2015–16 +1.1/+0.8 and 2023–24 +0.7/+0.3.
- So every model keeps coastal warmth above what the failed years had. Model rainfall z is ≈ +2.2 (13/13 wet in DJF, 6/6 in MAM), though the 1° grid does not resolve the coastal plain.

Dec–Apr is the core coastal rainy season and the more conservative window for a high rating, since May depends on decay rate (models +1.2 to +6.0 °C in May).

**Conditional:** the rating assumes the coastal warmth persists; recheck with the October initialization. The colleague's "will definitely happen, with intensity similar to 1982–83/1997–98" is stronger than the map claims. The tier is confidence in shifted odds, not certainty, and the map makes no magnitude claims.

**v6 (24 Sep 2026, approved by Zeke): observed hit rates.** Each region was checked against the 8 strong El Niños since 1957 (NDJ ONI ≥ 1.5), using a spec pre-registered after statistics and ENSO reviewer passes. Main data are GPCC v2025, Berkeley Earth and GHCN-D stations. Full details are in `../hit_rates/METHODS.md`. Changes:
- *N & Central India, weaker monsoon Jun–Sep 2027:* **removed**. The decay-year monsoon was dry in only 1 of 8 events (median 108% of normal). The dry signal belongs to the developing year (8 of 8), which is 2026 and already past.
- *Yangtze:* downgraded from med-high to **medium ⚠** and relabelled "Jun–Jul 2027". Observed record: 4 of 8 for Jun–Aug (pre-registered), 6 of 8 for Jun–Jul (checked post hoc).
- *Southern Mekong, drought Mar–May 2027:* **added** at medium, with a hand-drawn polygon (0.8° buffer). Observed 7 of 8, median 71% of normal. Models 4 of 6 (not significant), so it is indicative like the other hand-drawn regions.
- *Subtitle:* now "…how often each signal appeared in the 8 strong El Niños since 1957".
- Mekong label placed over India to avoid the Sri Lanka and Yangtze labels.
- Current ⚠ regions: SE Australia, S California/US SW/N Mexico, Yangtze.

**v6.1 (24 Sep 2026, approved by Zeke): N California, wet Dec–Mar, added at medium** (previously an unshaded note).
- Shape: the pre-registered model-test box clipped to California. Models 13/13 in that box.
- Observed: 6/8 strong events (GPCC), including 2015–16 at 120% when SoCal missed. The La Niña caveat (7/12 on the same side) is in the post.
- The NA close-up's italic "unshaded" note was replaced by the region.
- Global-map label sits over the Great Plains to avoid the SoCal/BC label stack.

**v6.2 (24 Sep 2026, approved by Zeke): ⚠ applied consistently.** The flag now means the labelled-season signal underperformed in 2015–16 or 2023–24 (below the neutral-year median in the expected direction; hit_rates/derived/hit_events.csv).
- *Removed:* SE Australia. Sep–Nov was very dry in both 2015 (44%) and 2023 (74%); the old flag came from the Dec–Feb 2023–24 reversal, which is outside the label window.
- *Added:* NE Brazil (Mar–May 2024 at 100%, 67th percentile) and Central America & S Caribbean (Dec–Feb 2015–16 at the neutral median).
- *Not flagged, by author decision:* SE South America (2023–24 at 100%, 34th percentile), because the season average masks local floods; and Peru (per v5.3).
- *Current ⚠:* S California/SW US/N Mexico, Yangtze, NE Brazil, Central America & S Caribbean.
- The v5.3 "current ⚠" list above is superseded.

**v6.3 (24 Sep 2026, Zeke):** the ⚠ glyph is removed from all region labels and legends, because it duplicated the dashed outline. The dashed outline alone now marks underperforming regions, on the global map, the NA close-up and the three regional close-ups. The semantics are unchanged (see v6.2).

**v6.4 (24 Sep 2026, approved by Zeke; suggestion from a Chilean colleague):**
- *Altiplano: dry, Dec–Mar, medium.* Hand-traced plateau outline, trimmed south of Lake Titicaca (≈16°S), where the literature finds a weak or reversed signal. Models are robust across the plateau (93% of cells).

- *Label moves:* SE South America's label moved to the Atlantic side, and the Peru and Altiplano labels were swapped, to avoid crossing leaders.

**New figures (24 Sep 2026):**
- `make_regional_maps.py` produces `elnino_2026_impacts_map_{indo_pacific,africa,south_america}`. Tiers and shapes are read from `make_impacts_map.py`, and footer numbers are read from `hit_rates/derived/hit_summary.csv` and `hit_events.csv` at render time.

## Regional graphics (23 Sep 2026)

**`elnino_2026_impacts_map_north_america` (make_impacts_map_na.py).** A close-up of the global v5.1 map. Tiers, flags and shapes are read from `make_impacts_map.py` and `model_polygons.json`, so the two cannot drift apart. Additions:
- An unshaded N California note (models lean wet; weak long-record link).
- A Hawaii inset. Because the model-robust area covers the whole inset, the islands themselves are shaded in the tier colour.
- A footer with the SoCal hindcast numbers (2015–16: 9/10 models wet, observed 60–68% of normal) and the out-of-range caveat.

**`elnino_2026_europe_signal` (make_europe_signal.py): an explainer, not an impacts map.** No European region reaches the global map's bar:
- **Literature** (research/lit_europe.md, 15 DOIs Crossref-verified): low / low-medium. The canonical late-winter cold-north/wet-south pattern depends on a sudden stratospheric warming (Ineson & Scaife 2009), and the link may have weakened since the 1970s (Ivasić et al. 2021).
- **Models:** pre-registered tests (`model_patterns/europe.py`, `derived/europe_table.csv`) found no robust region. Moderate leans: UK and central Europe wet in Oct–Dec (12/13, z ≈ +0.3); Scandinavia cold in Jan–Feb (11/11, z −0.56). Central and eastern Europe lean *wet* in Jan–Feb, opposite to the textbook. Robust cells cover 8% of European land (Oct–Dec rain), 2% (Jan–Feb rain) and 0% (Jan–Feb temperature).
- **NAO chart:** every winter with NDJ ONI ≥ 1.5 since 1950 (CPC ONI and NAO, fetched live). Split 4 positive / 4 negative, mean +0.09. An earlier draft that showed only the four strongest post-1980 events (3/4 positive) was replaced because that selection overstated a positive-NAO tendency.
- All numbers on the graphic come from the data files.

**`elnino_2026_model_precip_pct` / `elnino_2026_model_temperature` (make_model_anomaly_maps.py).** Multi-model mean maps for Oct–Dec 2026 and Dec–Feb 2027 (NMME + C3S) and Mar–May 2027 (NMME only). The stippling is **sign-only**: ≥80% of models share the sign of the mean. That is deliberately looser than the impacts map's robustness bar (which also needs |z| ≥ 0.5), so dots cover much more area.
- **Precipitation:** % = mean anomaly / GPCP 1991–2020 climatology. Anomalies are relative to each model's hindcast climate. Only *land* cells below 0.5 mm/day are masked, so the (real) large percentage increases over the Pacific cold tongue stay visible.
- **Temperature:** vs a common 1991–2020 baseline. Each model is shifted by the ERA5 trend × (2006.0 − its baseline midpoint). The long-term trend is NOT removed, so these show "hotter than normal". CanESM5 and CESM1 are excluded (undocumented baselines), leaving 11 models, or 4 in Mar–May, where 80% means all four agree.
- Latitude crop 58°S–78°N.
- `elnino_2026_australia_models` (make_australia_models.py) is a 2×3 Australia close-up: rain % and temperature for Sep–Nov, Dec–Feb and Mar–May. It imports `members()` and `agreement()` from make_model_anomaly_maps.py, so the methods are identical. Scales are narrower (±50%, ±2 °C). Regional checks (land means, cells ≥0.5 mm/day):
  - SE Australia (Vic/Tas) Sep–Nov: −12% (−0.23 mm/day), 12/13 models drier.
  - E NSW/Qld coast Sep–Nov: −17%, 12/13 drier.
  - N Australia Dec–Feb: −12% (−0.95 mm/day), 11/13 drier.
  - Central Australia Mar–May: +50%, but only +0.37 mm/day on a 0.73 mm/day climatology (5/6 NMME models). This is a percentage-of-arid-climatology effect and should not be read as a major autumn rain signal.
  - Because of this, the rain panels mask land below **1 mm/day** (DRY_MM; the global maps use 0.5), in all three seasons for consistency. That greys out most of the interior in spring and autumn.
- `elnino_2026_model_precip_pct_100` is the same figure on a ±100% scale. In both precipitation versions, displayed values are floored at −100%. A small area (0.3–4.3% of the mapped area, mostly ocean, computed in the script) has multi-model mean anomalies larger than the observed climatology, because model climates are wetter than GPCP along rain-band edges. The ±60% version was silently saturating these cells; the ±100% version exposed them as blank holes before the floor was added.

## Palette

Two sequential ramps (intensity = confidence, dark = high) on a light surface:
- Drought: #8C510A / #C4791C / #F4C154
- Flood: #0A5599 / #3F8FC5 / #7FC4EA

Validated 2026-08-13 with the dataviz skill's `validate_palette.js` (light mode): CVD separation PASS (worst adjacent pair ΔE 14.5 protan / 15.2 tritan), normal-vision floor PASS (15.1). The validator's categorical-scope lightness-band and chroma-floor checks flag the two lightest steps; these are intentional sequential-confidence steps (both ramps lightness-monotone), and the required relief for the contrast warning is provided by direct text labels on every region. The cross-ramp light pair (#F4C154 vs #7FC4EA) is hue-separated (brown vs blue) specifically for CVD safety.

**Colour semantics across the figure family (24 Sep 2026):**
- Blue is reserved for wet, brown/ochre for dry, red for warm and violet for cold.
- The hit grid's temperature scale was changed from blue–red to violet–red (#9E4AA0, #D5A6D6, #E6E3DD, #EA8466, #B2182B). Before that, "much colder" and "much wetter" were both blue.
- Within-row CVD separation passes (worst adjacent pair ΔE 14.5). Violet against the wet blues passes the normal-vision floor (ΔE 20.1 dark, 15.1 light).
- Cross-variable pairs are not CVD-separable: violet ≈ blue and dark red ≈ dark brown for deutan. Every row is labelled with its variable, so this is acceptable (agreed with Zeke).
- Any future "cold" region on the maps should use the violet ramp, not blue.

**`elnino_2026_forecast_octfeb_{indo_pacific,africa,south_america,north_america}` (make_regional_forecast_maps.py, 24 Sep 2026).** Oct 2026–Feb 2027 multi-model forecast maps: rain % of normal (13 models) and temperature °C vs 1991–2020 (11 models, including long-term warming), side by side. Projections and extents match the regional close-ups.
- *Oct–Feb construction:* per model, (3 × OND + 2 × JF)/5 from seasonal_anoms.nc. The GPCP climatology uses the same weighting.
- *Other methods:* as in make_model_anomaly_maps.py (dry-land mask < 0.5 mm/day, floor at −100%, sign-only 80% stippling).
- *Colours:* brown/blue for rain and violet/red for temperature, per the family colour rule.
- *Outlines:* all impact-map regions, dashed where flagged.
- *`_clean` variants* (for standalone sharing): the same maps without impact-region outlines, and with a subtitle that doesn't reference the impacts map. "As a strong El Niño develops" rests on CPC JJA 2026 ONI = +1.80.
- *Rendering:* fields are re-centred on the map meridian, subset to the window (+35° lon, +20° lat) and contoured in projected space (transform_first), because the full global grid gave streaks in the azimuthal projections. Outlines are clipped to the window.

## Known limitations

- Region polygons are hand-digitized approximations for communication, not analysis products; extents are indicative (buffered/smoothed shapely polygons; coordinates in the script).
- Label proximity issues from v3 resolved in v4; labels re-laid out for v5.
- Every SST/probability number in the accompanying text must name index type (conventional vs relative), product, period, and baseline per the project rule in `../research/local-pipeline-state.md`.
